findings.issue: Still open from the last review: proof-1 starts with no top padding, so its first line ('Orders start at 50 pieces per style in each colour.') sits on the section's top edge, directly under m2's last item, and the section label covers it. proof-2 does the same under proof-1-charts, where 'Once you've approved the sample…' is cut by its label.
findings.reference: The competitor's text sections leave the same clear gap above their first line as between all its other sections.
findings.fix: Keep the normal .block padding-block-start (calc(var(--section-space) / 2)) on .block--proof (band variant) when it follows a section with the same background, instead of setting it to 0. This covers proof-1 under m2 and proof-2 under proof-1-charts.

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: on phones, proof-1 and proof-2 also start flush with their top edge, so 'Orders start at 50 pieces…' and 'Once you've approved the sample…' touch the section above and sit under its label.
findings.reference: The competitor's mobile text blocks have the same top gap as every other section.
findings.fix: Same fix as on desktop: give .block--proof its normal top padding when it follows a neighbour with the same background.

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: the white/tint alternation breaks after m3. m2, proof-1, proof-1-charts (white, with only an inset tinted card) and proof-2 are four white sections in a row, at both widths.
findings.reference: The competitor separates neighbouring sections by their background.
findings.fix: Have the template's alternation treat the proof-1 / proof-1-charts / proof-2 group as one plain section and tint it through --section-tint. The page then reads m2 (white), proof group (tint), process-1 (white), related (tint), cta-steps (white).

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: the section title 'From your brief to shipment: the typical order path' is a small body-size bold line, so the left column has no real heading and stands mostly empty beside the six steps.
findings.reference: The competitor's step modules put a section heading over the steps, at heading weight and size.
findings.fix: Render the process list variant's title as the section h2. The template fits it like the other headings and starts it on the content's left edge, so the list stands beside a real heading.

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: on phones the order path opens with a small paragraph ('From your brief to shipment: the typical order path') instead of a heading, so it reads as part of the related block above rather than as its own section.
findings.reference: The competitor's mobile steps stack under a section heading.
findings.fix: Same as on desktop: set the process list variant's title as the section h2.

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: two iconList sections of the same shape stand one under the other. m3 and then m2 each have a heading on the left and a column of check-marked short items on the right, and only the background changes.
findings.reference: The competitor doesn't repeat a module back to back, and the site's own rule says one of two same-shaped neighbours is set out differently.
findings.fix: When two iconList sections are neighbours, let the template set one of them in a different arrangement, e.g. m2's items as a two-column grid under its heading.

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: the heading 'Quality Claims, Returns and Outside Vendor Liability' breaks over four uneven lines and leaves 'Outside' alone on the third line. m2's heading likewise leaves 'Shipping' alone on a line.
findings.reference: The competitor's section headings break into even lines.
findings.fix: Apply text-wrap: balance to the section h2 in the template's heading fit. Its lines then break evenly without changing the fitted size.

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: the heading 'Related products and services' sits over a single link, 'Privacy Policy', which is neither a product nor a service. The same happens on mobile.
findings.reference: The competitor's related-link blocks list pages that match their heading.
findings.fix: In Site Factory, either link the order-related product or service pages here, or retitle the block to fit its link (e.g. 'Related policies').
